q: 1. In slope deflection method, the unknown rotations at various joints are determined by considering
explain: In the slope-deflection method, unknown joint rotations are solved for by writing and satisfying the moment equilibrium equations at each joint.

q: 2. In slope deflection method, the end moments for any members are expressed .............
options: in terms of the unknown end reactions
explain: In slope-deflection method, member end moments are expressed as functions of the unknown joint rotations and settlements (translations) — described in the source options as 'unknown end reactions'.

q: 4. For a conjugate beam, the fixed end of a real beam corresponds to
explain: A fixed end (zero slope, zero deflection) in the real beam becomes a free end in the conjugate beam, per the standard conjugate-beam correspondence rules.

q: 5. For a strongest rectangular beam cut from a circular log, the ratio of the width and depth is
explain: For maximum section modulus from a circular log of diameter D, the optimal condition gives depth d = D/√3 and width b = D×√(2/3), yielding a width-to-depth ratio of 1/√2 ≈ 0.707.

q: 6. The effect of arching a beam is
explain: By 'arching' a beam (curving it to more closely follow the funicular/thrust line for the given loads), bending moment throughout the member is reduced compared to a straight beam.

q: 7. Internal forces at every cross section in a arch are
options: normal thrust, shear force and bending moment
explain: In general, an arch cross-section resists three internal force components: normal (axial) thrust, shear force, and bending moment, unless the arch axis coincides exactly with the thrust line.

q: 8. Due to rise in temperature, in a three hinged arch, induced stress is
explain: Because a three-hinged arch is statically determinate, a temperature change causes free thermal expansion/contraction (accommodated by hinge rotations) without inducing any internal stress.

q: 9. If a three hinged parabolic arch carries a udl over the entire span, then any section of the arch is subjected to
options: normal thrust, shear force and bending moment
explain: A parabolic arch under a matching uniformly distributed load has its axis coincide exactly with the funicular (thrust) line everywhere, so every section carries pure normal thrust with zero shear and moment.

q: 12. The specimen in Charpy impact test is supported as a
explain: In the Charpy impact test, the notched specimen is supported horizontally at both ends (as a simply supported beam) and struck at the center opposite the notch.

q: 13. For a beam of uniform strength, if depth is constant
explain: For a rectangular section with constant depth d, since σ ∝ M/(bd²), keeping stress constant with fixed d requires width b to vary directly proportional to M.

q: 14. The maximum deflection due to uniformly distributed load w per unit length over entire span of a cantilever of length l and of flexural rigidity EI is
explain: The standard formula for maximum (tip) deflection of a cantilever under UDL over its full length is wl⁴/8EI.

q: 15. The maximum deflection of a simply supported beam of span L, carrying an isolated load at the center of the span
explain: The standard formula for maximum deflection of a simply supported beam under a central point load W is WL³/48EI.

q: 16. The ratio of the deflections of the free end of a cantilever due to an isolated load at 1/3rd and 2/3rd of the span is
explain: Using the standard cantilever deflection formula for a load at distance a from the fixed end (deflection at tip involves a²(3L-a)), evaluating for a=L/3 versus a=2L/3 and taking the ratio gives 2/7.

q: 17. The ratio of the length and diameter of a simply supported uniform circular beam which experiences maximum bending stress equal to tensile stress due to same load at its mid span is
explain: Equating the bending stress formula (from flexure) to the direct tensile stress formula (from axial elongation test) for the same circular bar and load leads to a length-to-diameter ratio of 1/2.

q: 18. The ratio of the length and depth of a simply supported rectangular beam which experiences maximum bending stress equal to tensile stress, due to same load at its mid span is
explain: Similarly equating bending stress to tensile stress for a rectangular bar of the same load gives a length-to-depth ratio of 2/3.

q: 19. Beams of uniform strength are preferred to those of uniform section because these are economical for
explain: Beams of uniform strength save material by removing unnecessary cross-section where bending moment is low, making them more economical particularly for lighter load applications where material savings matter proportionally more.
